usageNotes: Use this to enable or adjust the per-VM firewall and its behavior on a PVE remote managed by PDM. The firewall must first be enabled via `enable: true` before any rules take effect; toggling options on a disabled firewall has no live impact. Pass `digest` (retrieved from the corresponding GET) to guard against concurrent edits overwriting each other.

examples.summary: Enable the VM firewall with DROP default policies, info-level inbound logging, and IP filters on

tips: Enabling `ipfilter` without adding explicit IP addresses to the corresponding ipfilter-net ipset will still apply sane default restrictions (MAC-derived IPv6 link-local), but no custom allow rules — verify behavior before applying to production VMs.
The `delete` array accepts field names (e.g. `["policy_in", "log_level_out"]`) to reset individual options back to their defaults without sending a full config payload.
Returns null on success; any non-2xx response indicates failure — check PDM logs for detail since no error body is guaranteed.
The `node` param is optional; omit it to let PDM resolve the VM's current node automatically via the remote cluster state.
